title: Laboratory Equipment Integration Database — Overview and definition
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Device drivers, connection methods, calibration procedures, and compatibility records. The Laboratory Equipment Integration Database is the plumbing manual for automated labs: how to connect each instrument (drivers, protocols, cables), how to calibrate it, which devices work together, and the troubleshooting for when they do not. Lab equipment spans decades of vendors and interfaces — each record documents one device's integration completely so the next lab does not rediscover it.

title: Laboratory Equipment Integration Database — Knowledge: technical reference
body: Signature edition. Original Signature methods, framings, and analyses developed for the JAH system, labeled Signature throughout; never mixed with public-harvest records. Integration layers: physical (cables, connectors, power), link (serial settings: baud/data/parity/stop; USB classes; TCP ports; GPIB addresses), protocol (command syntax, response parsing, error codes), driver (vendor SDK, open-source alternative, direct implementation), application (the lab software's device abstraction). Calibration: against traceable standards (NIST-traceable buffers/weights), schedule per device class, records with as-found/as-left values, out-of-tolerance handling. Compatibility: tested pairs (device A + software B + OS C); version pins; known conflicts. Troubleshooting taxonomy: no-communication (cable/port/settings), wrong-data (protocol mismatch, byte order), drift (calibration/fouling), intermittent (grounding/EMI, documented fixes). Documentation: one page per device with everything above — the record format.
